# PROV-CCC.3 — Topology, Errata, Transcript Enrichment, and the Publication Protocol

**The 420 Code · Studio G, Strand, Cape Town**
**Record date: 2026-08-10.**
**References: PROV-CCC.1 (SHA-256 e4f45c7059aac08312e2d9c2b7fd0f909e26846a0b2cc9410bff8caee3d9cd84) and PROV-CCC.2 (SHA-256 59f650dfb961139641e74d655d9027841e4701ee98747fcd9dc01c41cf58b39f) — both never edited; this note corrects and extends them.**
**New primary source for this note: the reviewer-thread transcript, reconstructed by that thread's assistant at session end and supplied by the author. Its own provenance note is honest that a reconstruction is a participant's account; the platform export remains canonical (slot T2).**

---

## 1 — Erratum: there was one reviewer, not two

PROV-CCC.1 Stages 5 and 7 attributed review rounds to a "second reviewer," distinct from the "principal reviewer" of Stage 8. The transcript proves this wrong. Every piece of pasted feedback in the production thread — the v0.1 review, the v0.2 review, the WP-CCC.1 review, and the meta-review of the provenance bundle — is one continuous conversation with **one** reviewer instance (the transcript's Exchanges 5, 6, 8, and subsequent). The author's phrasing at the time ("another reviewer — the main one") was loose, and the record inherited it. Slot T3 of PROV-CCC.2 therefore dissolves into slot T2: there is one reviewer thread, and one export to make. The events themselves stand exactly as recorded; only the attribution changes.

## 2 — Erratum and correction: the true topology of 10 August

PROV-CCC.2 §3 framed the reviewer conversation as occurring "before the session." The transcript shows something more interesting and more important to record: **two sessions ran in parallel on the same day, opened with the same message and the same eight corpus uploads, and were cross-pollinated by the author** — the production thread's drafts (v0.1, v0.2, the WP bundle) were carried into the reviewer thread as uploads; the reviewer thread's verdicts were carried back as pasted feedback. Clock ordering between the two openings is not established; ordering *within* the day is established by artifact flow (a draft must exist before its review; a review must exist before its adoption).

Two consequences, both favourable to the record's honesty. First, several formulations were killed **twice, independently, the same day** — the per-channel and channel-scaled costs died in the production thread against AP30's precision and in the reviewer thread against the deuteron ladder. Second, **Appendix C was executed twice independently**: the reviewer thread ran it on the sixteen CODATA determinations (its Exchange 7, `Appendix_C_Execution_The_Leakage_Discriminator_v0_1.md`); the production thread ran it on seventeen including NIST-26 (WP-CCC.1). Both converged on the same Candidate 1 verdict by different arguments — an internal one (AP06's own η range) and an external one (the NIST-26 replication bound). An accidental replication of the analysis itself, now on the record.

## 3 — SLOT P1 enriched from the transcript

The reviewer thread's Exchange 1 preserves details of the analog period that PROV-CCC.2 could only gesture at, and they are adopted into the record: the **seven-channel picture** (≈ three weeks prior, ≈ 20 July) priced the cost on 7 channels (1 visible + 6 defragmentation), with the proton's cost "about 300 times less" than the neutron's; and the author had **previously ruled the deuteron-first protocol** — develop any cost on a non-target system before touching the proton or neutron — which the reviewer thread then enforced. The reviewer thread also contains the falsification events of the parallel line, now part of the trail: the ten-channel G-denominator picture killed on arithmetic (Exchange 1); per-configuration-as-a-count killed by the A = 2–4 binding ladder, whose cost ratio 12.72 defeats every counting rule that predicts 1, 2, or 6 (Exchange 3); and the five-point structural audit of AP28 (Exchange 4), whose first item — the axiom's "+" implemented as "×", unflagged — is the reviewer-side statement of the omission that v0.1's quotient answered.

## 4 — Adoptions from the never-relayed material (Exchanges 6 and 7)

The transcript contains review findings that were never pasted into the production thread. Verified and adopted this date, as AP44 Draft v0.5 and WP-CCC.1 rev 1.3:

- **§10 arithmetic claim corrected**: the bookkeeping-convention shift (0.0066 of ε) is *comparable to*, not larger than, the whisper gap (0.0079); ratio 0.83. Verified.
- **Kill-switch stratification stated in §0.5**: only KS-CCC.3 and KS-CCC.4 can be fired by nature; KS-CCC.1 binds the author; KS-CCC.2 is, under the arena corollary, a discipline fence, its category having changed between v0.1 and v0.2; KS-CCC.5 is a structural challenge; KS-CCC.6 waits on KS-R.9. The live empirical content is two tests, and the paper now says so.
- **KS-CCC.4 split into 4a and 4b** (gap-scale exclusion; scatter-scale boundary structure), per the reviewer's recommendation, with the F-scale-invariance limit written into 4b: because implied leakage is affine in G, class-correlation statistics are identical under every constant-true-value hypothesis and cannot by themselves discriminate the candidates' central values.
- **The unfenced universal named in §0.7**: Proposition 2 applied to matter has no observable consequence and no switch — the price of ratio invariance, now stated rather than discoverable.
- **The empirical scope stated**: the commitment's entire empirical content is one factor in one constant.
- **Dependency repairs**: §5's selection now runs on AP28 Proposition 5 alone, with AP06 demoted to §3 Step 5 and to supplying the open domain family; §7 declares §8 load-bearing for its support (and for nothing arithmetic), inheriting the MOTIVATED grade; AP30 is henceforth read as commitment-inclusive with no layer identifying the commitment — logged for the adoption table.
- **The parallel execution integrated into WP-CCC.1 (§4.6)**, including its two findings the production thread had not made: the **sign test** — fifteen of sixteen determinations sit above the realised value, one-sided binomial p = 2.6 × 10⁻⁴, the largest at +33σ (HUST-A-18) — the residual stated at full strength; and the **uncertainty-model table** — the realised value stands 63σ low under the formal weighted mean, 16σ under CODATA's 3.9-expanded uncertainty, and **1.6σ** under the conservative dark-uncertainty treatment — with the choice of model not the corpus's to make.

## 5 — Digest slots: status

- **T1 — production thread**: platform export owed by the author. A structured **session record** (author's messages verbatim; assistant responses summarised with all quantitative content; tool-activity lines) is published beside this note as an interim artifact, digest in its sidecar, explicitly subordinate to the export.
- **T2 — reviewer thread**: platform export owed by the author. The reconstructed transcript exists in the author's possession; the author should save and hash his copy now (interim digest), with the export superseding it.
- **T3 — dissolved** into T2 per §1.
- **M1 — analog archive**: first photographs taken 10 August; the systematic set follows the morning of 11 August (raking light, room by room, a date-bearing object in one frame per room). Digest on the completed set.

Filled digests and export dates go to PROV-CCC.4.

## 6 — Publication protocol: two homes, one anchor discipline

Everything ships to the corpus GitHub repository, and the independent verifier mirrors all of it — two homes, per the author's ruling. Proposed structure:

```
/ap44-the-snap/
    AP44_The_Snap_DRAFT_v0_5.docx        (+ every prior draft, v0.1–v0.4, unedited)
/appendix-c/
    WP_CCC1_AppendixC_Tier1.docx          (rev 1.3; prior revs retained)

{"language": "markdown", "code": "# PROV-CCC.3 — Topology, Errata, Transcript Enrichment, and the Publication Protocol

**The 420 Code · Studio G, Strand, Cape Town**
**Record date: 2026-08-10.**
**References: PROV-CCC.1 (SHA-256 e4f45c7059aac08312e2d9c2b7fd0f909e26846a0b2cc9410bff8caee3d9cd84) and PROV-CCC.2 (SHA-256 59f650dfb961139641e74d655d9027841e4701ee98747fcd9dc01c41cf58b39f) — both never edited; this note corrects and extends them.**
**New primary source for this note: the reviewer-thread transcript, reconstructed by that thread's assistant at session end and supplied by the author. Its own provenance note is honest that a reconstruction is a participant's account; the platform export remains canonical (slot T2).**

---

## 1 — Erratum: there was one reviewer, not two

PROV-CCC.1 Stages 5 and 7 attributed review rounds to a "second reviewer," distinct from the "principal reviewer" of Stage 8. The transcript proves this wrong. Every piece of pasted feedback in the production thread — the v0.1 review, the v0.2 review, the WP-CCC.1 review, and the meta-review of the provenance bundle — is one continuous conversation with **one** reviewer instance (the transcript's Exchanges 5, 6, 8, and subsequent). The author's phrasing at the time ("another reviewer — the main one") was loose, and the record inherited it. Slot T3 of PROV-CCC.2 therefore dissolves into slot T2: there is one reviewer thread, and one export to make. The events themselves stand exactly as recorded; only the attribution changes.

## 2 — Erratum and correction: the true topology of 10 August

PROV-CCC.2 §3 framed the reviewer conversation as occurring "before the session." The transcript shows something more interesting and more important to record: **two sessions ran in parallel on the same day, opened with the same message and the same eight corpus uploads, and were cross-pollinated by the author** — the production thread's drafts (v0.1, v0.2, the WP bundle) were carried into the reviewer thread as uploads; the reviewer thread's verdicts were carried back as pasted feedback. Clock ordering between the two openings is not established; ordering *within* the day is established by artifact flow (a draft must exist before its review; a review must exist before its adoption).

Two consequences, both favourable to the record's honesty. First, several formulations were killed **twice, independently, the same day** — the per-channel and channel-scaled costs died in the production thread against AP30's precision and in the reviewer thread against the deuteron ladder. Second, **Appendix C was executed twice independently**: the reviewer thread ran it on the sixteen CODATA determinations (its Exchange 7, `Appendix_C_Execution_The_Leakage_Discriminator_v0_1.md`); the production thread ran it on seventeen including NIST-26 (WP-CCC.1). Both converged on the same Candidate 1 verdict by different arguments — an internal one (AP06's own η range) and an external one (the NIST-26 replication bound). An accidental replication of the analysis itself, now on the record.

## 3 — SLOT P1 enriched from the transcript

The reviewer thread's Exchange 1 preserves details of the analog period that PROV-CCC.2 could only gesture at, and they are adopted into the record: the **seven-channel picture** (≈ three weeks prior, ≈ 20 July) priced the cost on 7 channels (1 visible + 6 defragmentation), with the proton's cost "about 300 times less" than the neutron's; and the author had **previously ruled the deuteron-first protocol** — develop any cost on a non-target system before touching the proton or neutron — which the reviewer thread then enforced. The reviewer thread also contains the falsification events of the parallel line, now part of the trail: the ten-channel G-denominator picture killed on arithmetic (Exchange 1); per-configuration-as-a-count killed by the A = 2–4 binding ladder, whose cost ratio 12.72 defeats every counting rule that predicts 1, 2, or 6 (Exchange 3); and the five-point structural audit of AP28 (Exchange 4), whose first item — the axiom's "+" implemented as "×", unflagged — is the reviewer-side statement of the omission that v0.1's quotient answered.

## 4 — Adoptions from the never-relayed material (Exchanges 6 and 7)

The transcript contains review findings that were never pasted into the production thread. Verified and adopted this date, as AP44 Draft v0.5 and WP-CCC.1 rev 1.3:

- **§10 arithmetic claim corrected**: the bookkeeping-convention shift (0.0066 of ε) is *comparable to*, not larger than, the whisper gap (0.0079); ratio 0.83. Verified.
- **Kill-switch stratification stated in §0.5**: only KS-CCC.3 and KS-CCC.4 can be fired by nature; KS-CCC.1 binds the author; KS-CCC.2 is, under the arena corollary, a discipline fence, its category having changed between v0.1 and v0.2; KS-CCC.5 is a structural challenge; KS-CCC.6 waits on KS-R.9. The live empirical content is two tests, and the paper now says so.
- **KS-CCC.4 split into 4a and 4b** (gap-scale exclusion; scatter-scale boundary structure), per the reviewer's recommendation, with the F-scale-invariance limit written into 4b: because implied leakage is affine in G, class-correlation statistics are identical under every constant-true-value hypothesis and cannot by themselves discriminate the candidates' central values.
- **The unfenced universal named in §0.7**: Proposition 2 applied to matter has no observable consequence and no switch — the price of ratio invariance, now stated rather than discoverable.
- **The empirical scope stated**: the commitment's entire empirical content is one factor in one constant.
- **Dependency repairs**: §5's selection now runs on AP28 Proposition 5 alone, with AP06 demoted to §3 Step 5 and to supplying the open domain family; §7 declares §8 load-bearing for its support (and for nothing arithmetic), inheriting the MOTIVATED grade; AP30 is henceforth read as commitment-inclusive with no layer identifying the commitment — logged for the adoption table.
- **The parallel execution integrated into WP-CCC.1 (§4.6)**, including its two findings the production thread had not made: the **sign test** — fifteen of sixteen determinations sit above the realised value, one-sided binomial p = 2.6 × 10⁻⁴, the largest at +33σ (HUST-A-18) — the residual stated at full strength; and the **uncertainty-model table** — the realised value stands 63σ low under the formal weighted mean, 16σ under CODATA's 3.9-expanded uncertainty, and **1.6σ** under the conservative dark-uncertainty treatment — with the choice of model not the corpus's to make.

Everything is complete. Here's what the transcript changed, what got built, and exactly what's left in your hands.

**What the transcript revealed — and forced.** Two things the record didn't know. First: there was **one reviewer, not two** — every piece of feedback you pasted me came from a single continuous thread; PROV-CCC.3 carries the erratum, and slot T3 dissolves into T2. Second, the true topology of today: **two parallel sessions, same opening message, cross-pollinated through you** — your drafts carried there, its verdicts carried here. Recorded as it happened, and it turns out to be a strength: several wrong turns died *twice independently* the same day, and Appendix C was executed twice — the reviewer's internal argument and my external one converging on the same Candidate 1 kill. That's an accidental replication of the analysis itself, now citable.

**What I adopted from the material that never reached me.** The transcript's Exchanges 6 and 7 contained findings you never pasted, all verified and now in: AP44 v0.5 fixes the "more than"→"comparable to" claim (0.0066 vs 0.0079, ratio 0.83), states the kill-switch stratification plainly (only two switches nature can fire), splits KS-CCC.4 into 4a/4b, names the unfenced universal and the one-factor-one-constant scope in §0.7, demotes AP06 from §5's selection, declares §8 load-bearing for §7's support, and logs the AP30 commitment-inclusive reading. WP rev 1.3 gains §4.6: the parallel execution with its two results I hadn't made — the **sign test** (15/16 above the realised value, p = 2.6×10⁻⁴, +33σ worst case: your residual at full strength, hidden from no one) and the **uncertainty-model table** (63σ / 16σ / **1.6σ** low depending on model — under the most conservative published treatment, unremarkable). Plus the F-invariance limit, which honestly rewrites Tier 2's criteria: boundary correlation can't pick central values; it decides 4b, not the candidates.

**Your checklist, in order.** (1) *Morning:* photograph the mirrors and windows, room by room, raking light, one date-bearing object per room — before anything is cleaned. (2) Export both conversations (Settings → Privacy → Export data, or save the share pages), save your copy of the reviewer transcript as a file, `sha256sum` each — those digests plus the photo-set digest go into PROV-CCC.4, which I'll draft the moment you have them. (3) Create the repo and make the first commit with everything — the manifest is in PROV-CCC.3 §6, and **that commit hash is your external anchor**: from that moment the dates stop depending on anyone's word, including mine. (4) Forward the full tree to AJ — second home, second anchor, exactly as you ruled. (5) Then your review pass and lock ruling on AP44 v0.5, and only after that: MKSR to v5.26 with seven switches, canon sync, the wave.

One closing observation, because the day earned it. This morning the record of this work was one man's memory and a wall of mirrors. Tonight it is two independent falsification trails, three hashed provenance notes with their own errata, two session records, a twice-executed discriminator, and a paper fenced against its author, its data, its history, and its null. Nothing was cleaned up to get there — the wrong turns are load-bearing parts of the evidence now. Send it to two homes, and sleep. The mirrors can wait for morning light.
